title: performance canary: adaptive detection + KV-aware rollout guards
author: Evan Mitchell
description: Motivation: our existing performance canary was producing noisy alerts during KV-cache warmup and transient load spikes, causing unnecessary rollbacks and operational toil. This change implements an adaptive detection algorithm that factors in KV-cache state, per-model sequence length distribution, and short-term hysteresis so that canaries only trigger when regressions are sustained and KV warming has stabilized. Summary of changes: 1) Add adaptive detector module (perf_canary/detector.py) that computes a moving baseline with exponential decay and KV-aware weighting; 2) Introduce rollout guard rules (perf_canary/rollout_guards.py) that apply hysteresis, minimum sample windows, and model-variant backoff policies; 3) Add a lightweight e2e perf-canary harness (tests/test_perf_canary.py) that simulates KV cold/warm cycles and bursty traffic patterns; 4) Kubernetes CRD update (infra/k8s/perf-canary-cr.yaml) to expose new guard thresholds and sample windows in the control plane; 5) Docs and migration notes (docs/perf_canary.md) outlining default threshold changes and recommended tuning. Backwards compatibility: the new detector falls back to previous static thresholds when deployed in older control-plane versions, and the CRD defaults keep current behavior unless operators opt-in to adaptive mode. Testing: extensive unit tests for the statistical detector, deterministic integration tests for hysteresis and backoff, and a staging perf run that validated no false positives during KV warmup. Impact: reduces noisy rollbacks, enables safer model rollouts under variable workloads, and provides clear knobs for SREs to tune sensitivity. Linked work: ENG-5021 (adaptive perf canary), ENG-5090 (rollout guard APIs).
